items.title: Section: Cursing One's Own Parents — Harsh Words at Their Gravest

items.zh: 或破壞他，令離善友、父母、男女，破和合僧。若離間語，能引殺生、或不與取、或欲邪行。如前所說道理應知。如是一切，由事重故，名重離間語。復次，若於父母及餘師長發麁惡言。由事重故，名重麁惡語。或以不實不真妄語，現前毀罵呵責於他。由事重故，名重麁惡語。復次，凡諸綺語隨妄語等，此語輕重，如彼應知。若依鬪訟、諍競等事而發綺語，亦名為重。若以染污心，於能引無義外道典籍承誦、讚詠、廣為他說。由事重故，名重綺語。若於父母、眷屬、師長調弄輕笑，現作語言不近道理。亦由事重，名重綺語。
items.en: Or destroying another, causing them to be parted from good friends, parents, sons, or daughters, or splitting the harmonious community, or divisive speech capable of provoking killing, taking what is not given, or sexual misconduct, should be understood according to the principle already explained. All of this, through the gravity of the object, is called grave divisive speech. Moreover, directing coarse speech at one's parents or other teachers is, through the gravity of the object, called grave harsh speech. Reviling and reproaching another to their face with an untrue, unreal falsehood is, through the gravity of the object, called grave harsh speech. Moreover, idle chatter generally follows false speech in its gravity, as should be understood accordingly. Idle chatter arising from dispute and rivalry is likewise called grave. With a defiled mind, reciting, praising, and broadly expounding to others heretical texts capable of leading only to no benefit is, through the gravity of the object, called grave idle chatter. Mocking and ridiculing one's parents, family, or teachers with words far from reason is likewise, through the gravity of the object, called grave idle chatter.

items.title: Section: Wanting Recognition From Kings — And the Worst of All Wrong Views

items.zh: 復次，若於僧祇、佛靈廟等所有財寶，起貪欲心。由事重故，名重貪欲。若於己德起增上慢，自謂智者，乃於國王、大臣、豪貴、所尊師長及諸聰叡同梵行等，起增上欲，貪求利養，名重貪欲。復次，若於父母、眷屬、師長，起損害心。由事重故，名重瞋恚。又於無過、貧窮、孤苦、可傷愍者，起損害心。由事重故，名重瞋恚。又於誠心來歸投者及有恩所，起損害心。由事重故，名重瞋恚。復次，若於一切餘邪見中，諸有能謗一切邪見，此謗一切事門轉故，名重邪見。又若有見，謂無世間真阿羅漢、正至、正行，乃至廣說。如是邪見，由事重故，名重邪見。
items.en: Moreover, coveting property belonging to the monastic community or a Buddhist shrine is, through the gravity of the object, called grave covetousness. Harbouring an overreaching conceit about one's own virtue, considering oneself wise, and seeking recognition and support from kings, ministers, the powerful, respected teachers, and wise fellow practitioners, is called grave covetousness. Moreover, harbouring the wish to harm one's parents, family, or teachers is, through the gravity of the object, called grave malice. Harbouring the wish to harm one who is blameless, poor, orphaned, or pitiable is, through the gravity of the object, called grave malice. Harbouring the wish to harm one who has sincerely sought refuge or one to whom a debt of kindness is owed is, through the gravity of the object, called grave malice. Moreover, among all wrong views, the view capable of denying every single real thing turns upon every matter at once, and is called grave wrong view. The view holding that there is no true arhat, no one who has reached the destination, and no one of upright conduct in the world is, through the gravity of the object, called grave wrong view.

items.zh: 除如上說所有諸事，隨其所應，與彼相違，皆名為輕。

items.title: Section: Done Without Increasing, Increased Without Being Done

items.zh: 復次，殺生所引不善諸業，或有是作而非增長，或有增長而非是作，或有亦作亦復增長，或有非作亦非增長。初句，謂無識別童稚所作，或夢所作，或不思而作，或自無欲他逼令作。或有暫作，續即還起猛利悔心及厭患心，懇責遠離，正受律儀，令彼微薄，未與果報，便起世間離欲之道，損彼種子；次起出世永斷之道，害彼種子令無有餘。增長而非作者，謂如有一，為害生故，於長夜中數隨尋伺。由此因緣，彼遂增長殺生所引惡不善法，然不能作殺生之業。亦作亦增長者，謂除先所說作非增長、增長非作，所餘一切殺生業相。非作非增長者，謂除上爾所相。如是所餘不與取等乃至綺語，隨其所應，如殺應知。於貪欲、瞋恚、邪見中，無有第二增長而非作句，
items.en: Moreover, the unwholesome karma drawn forth by killing may be committed without increase, increased without being committed, both committed and increased, or neither committed nor increased. The first phrase refers to an act done by a discriminating-incapable child, done in a dream, done without intention, or done only because another, against one's own wish, compelled it. Or committed once, immediately followed by forceful regret and revulsion, sincere self-reproach and distancing, correctly undertaking the precept, weakening it, and before the fruit has ripened, giving rise to a worldly path of freedom from desire that damages its seed, and next a transcendent path of permanent severing that destroys that seed, leaving nothing remaining. Increased without being committed refers to one who, for the sake of harming a being, repeatedly examines and reflects on it through a long night of time; by this cause and condition, the unwholesome dharma drawn forth by killing increases, yet the karma of killing itself is never actually committed. Among covetousness, malice, and wrong view, there is no second phrase of increase without commission.

items.zh: 於初句中無有不思而作及他逼令作，餘如前說。

items.title: Section: Three Kinds of Fruit — A World Grown Barren by Its Own Killing

items.zh: 復次，若於殺生親近數習多所作故，生那落迦，是名殺生異熟果。若從彼沒，來生此間人同分中，壽量短促，是名殺生等流果。於外所得器世界中，飲食果藥皆少光澤，勢力異熟及與威德並皆微劣，消變不平，生長疾病。由此因緣，無量有情未盡壽量，非時中夭，是名殺生增上果。所餘業道，異熟、等流二果差別，如經應知。增上果，今當說。若器世間眾果尠少，果不滋長、果多朽壞、果不貞實，多無雨澤，諸果乾枯，或全無果。如是一切，名不與取增上果。若器世間多諸便穢泥糞不淨，臭處迫迮，多生不淨臭惡之物，凡諸所有皆不可樂。如是一切，名欲邪行增上果。
items.en: Moreover, if one closely cultivates, practices, and greatly pursues killing, one is born in the hells; this is called killing's ripening fruit. If, having fallen from there, one is reborn here among humankind, one's lifespan is short and truncated; this is called killing's outflow fruit. In the external material world thereby obtained, food, fruit, and medicine all carry little lustre, their potency and dominance feeble, transforming, once consumed and digested, so that the elements fall out of balance, giving rise to sickness; by this cause, countless beings, their lifespan not exhausted, die before their time. This is called killing's dominant fruit. If, in the material world, fruits are scarce, fail to ripen, rot easily, and are not genuine, and rain is frequently lacking, so that fruits wither, or there is no fruit at all — all of this is called the dominant fruit of taking what is not given. If, in the material world, there is much filth, mud, dung, and impurity, foul odours crowding every space, and unclean, foul things abound, nothing there being pleasant at all — all of this is called the dominant fruit of sexual misconduct.

blocks.text: Gravity in speech and thought, and the three kinds of result: ripening, corresponding, and dominant (the world we live in).

Master Cháng Bǎi: to revile those who should be respected is extreme; a false accusation adds the weight of a lie. Praising outsiders' texts that bring greed, hatred, and delusion is grave idle chatter.

Master Cháng Bǎi: strong desire for vast gain and offerings is grave covetousness. Reaching the first absorption and thinking it the first fruit is overestimation. The gravest wrong view denies all that really exists.

Master Cháng Bǎi: a child kills without an evil mind and does not dwell on it; a dreaming mind has little force; one who quickly repents weakens the karma. And "increased but not done": each time the thought of killing stirs, the evil grows, though no deed is done.

Master Cháng Bǎi: the ripening of killing is suffering in hell; the corresponding fruit is being killed oneself. The dominant fruit shapes the outer world, formed by beings' shared karma: food and medicine lose their power, and many die before their time.
The world we live in is partly the result of shared karma. Master Cháng Bǎi takes this literally; it also reads well as an ecological truth.

quiz.q: What makes divisive and harsh speech grave?
options: both depend on loudness and length, regardless of target or consequence
both on being written
breaking affection and harmony, provoking evil; addressing elders, or reviling with untruth
both on being said face to face
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: divisive speech is grave by what it brings about; to revile those who should be respected is extreme; and a false accusation adds the weight of a lie. The source has a further sentence on long-standing affection that the English lacks.

quiz.q: What counts as grave idle chatter?
options: following false speech; from dispute; reciting outsiders' texts with defiled mind; mocking elders
singing and jokes, anything pleasing, while outsiders' texts are scholarship and joking with parents filial
only writing poetry
only speaking before the Buddha
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: idle chatter is weighed like false speech; praising and spreading outsiders' texts that bring greed, hatred, and delusion is grave; and so is mocking parents and teachers. The defining word is 染汙心, a defiled mind, not the study of such texts as such.

quiz.q: What are the objects of grave covetousness and malice?
options: community and shrine property, conceited gain-seeking; parents, teachers, the blameless poor, refuge-seekers, benefactors
all wealth equally; only enemies for malice, hatred of foes being gravest, parents not being its objects
gods' wealth; gods
outsiders' wealth; outsiders
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: strong desire for vast and fine gain and offerings is grave covetousness; towards the pitiable one should feel compassion, yet one wishes to harm them. Gravity comes from the fitting response being reversed. The English "grave malice" is consistent here.

quiz.q: What does Master Cháng Bǎi give as an example of conceit about one's virtue?
options: taking the first absorption for the first fruit, claiming what is not attained
pride after the first fruit, conceit being only for noble ones, unrelated to claiming what is unattained
pride in wealth
pride in looks
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: for example, reaching the first absorption and thinking it the first fruit, a conceit of claiming what is unattained, from mistaking the signs. The treatise joins this to seeking recognition. The English "overreaching conceit" is a good rendering here.

quiz.q: Which wrong view is gravest, and why?
options: eternalism, clinging to a lasting self, annihilationism being lighter
view-attachment
precept-attachment
that denying all real things, cause, result, function; and denying any true arhat
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the gravest denies all phenomena, every real thing, cause, result, and function; grave because it denies all that really exists; and also the view that there is no true arhat in the world. This fits §46 of fascicle 59.

quiz.q: What cases are committed without increase?
options: killing planned for years, the calm at the act meaning no increase, reflection preventing it
killing to save others
a child, a dream, unthinking, compelled; or done once with instant regret and precepts
thinking in a dream without acting
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: a child kills without an evil mind and does not dwell on it; a dreaming mind has little force, tending to the neutral; one who quickly practices and gains absorption damages the seed. The English "discriminating-incapable child" is awkward but serves.

quiz.q: The English has "Among greed, hatred, and wrong view." What is the problem, and what is the reasoning?
options: no problem: they are the same as the poisons, and mental karma cannot increase, as the lecture says
these are the mental paths, elsewhere covetousness and malice; "greed" blurs with the poisons; for mental deeds to think is to do
the problem is "wrong view"
the problem is "second phrase"
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: for these, merely thinking so in the mind is already to do it, and so there is no second case of increase without commission. §6 and §15 distinguish covetousness from greed; this sentence uses the root-poison words for the mental paths, which obscures the point.

options: killing many without feeling, unrelated to dwelling on it, as only acts increase karma
long dwelling on harming, each stirring increasing it, with no actual deed
killing in a dream
killing under compulsion
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: each time the thought of killing stirs, the evil dharma of killing grows, though there is no actual deed; the seeds of hatred behind killing are undamaged. The English "a long night of time" for 長夜 is literal; it means a long time.

quiz.q: What are killing's ripening and outflow fruits?
options: a short life; the hells, ripening resembling the deed and outflow being heavier, unrelated to repeated practice
the world's food lacking lustre
untimely death of many
rebirth in the hells; a short life among humans
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the karma of killing ripens after time, into suffering in hell; the corresponding fruit resembles its cause, one who killed being killed. Note "outflow fruit" for 等流果 collides with "outflow" for 漏.

quiz.q: The English has "spoiling once transformed and causing imbalance." What is mistranslated?
options: nothing: food spoils easily, sickening those who eat it, 不平 meaning uneven taste, as the lecture says
消變 is digestion after eating, 不平 the elements' imbalance; "spoiling" makes the food rot
"sickness" is wrong
"transformed" is wrong
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: after digestion the food alters, the four elements become unequal, and illness spreads. So it concerns what happens in the body after eating. "Spoiling" moves the change to the food itself, and hides the causal chain to untimely death.

quiz.q: What forms the outer world's dominant fruit, and what are theft's and misconduct's?
options: decided by Maheśvara, unrelated to karma
by geography; serpents
mostly beings' past shared karma; theft brings scarce fruit, misconduct filth
by climate; drought
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the outer dominant fruit of the world is mostly formed by beings' past shared karma; since sexual desire is filthy, the world one lives in also becomes foul. The English "dominant fruit" for 增上果 is consistent.

quiz.q: Which of killing's fruits are a short life and untimely death?
options: ripening; outflow, the dominant fruit concerning only surroundings and never lifespan
both ripening
both outflow
outflow fruit; dominant fruit
quiz.why: Both involve early death but differ in mechanism: a personal short life corresponds to killing, while bad food and medicine in the outer world causing countless untimely deaths are the dominant fruit. Master Cháng Bǎi uses 中夭 for the first too; the treatise reserves it here for the second.
